title: Russia Kills 8, Injures 43 Across Ukraine on Independence Day with Missile-and-Drone Barrage
detail: Russia marked Ukraine's 35th Independence Day with a nationwide barrage overnight into August 24: two Oniks anti-ship missiles, six Kh-31P and Kh-59 guided air-launched missiles, and 143 drones (roughly a third jet-powered), striking 22 locations. Ukrainian air defense downed one Oniks, four of the six guided missiles, two Banderol munitions, and 109 drones. The attacks killed at least 8 people and injured 43 over the prior 24 hours. Kharkiv Oblast was hit hardest — 5 killed and 17 injured, including two women killed and an 11-year-old girl burned, with railway infrastructure struck in the Lozova community. Kramatorsk (Donetsk Oblast) saw 2 killed and 1 injured; Sumy Oblast recorded 1 killed and 12 injured across more than 50 strikes on 25 settlements; Zaporizhzhia Oblast logged 518 strikes on 38 settlements with 3 injured; Dnipropetrovsk Oblast saw roughly 30 drone, artillery, and guided-bomb attacks with 3 injured.

media.caption: Aftermath of a Russian drone attack on railway infrastructure in Lozova, Kharkiv Oblast, overnight Aug. 24

title: Russian Drone Strikes Residential Building in Central Chernihiv on Independence Day, Injuring 20
detail: A Russian Geran-5 jet-powered drone struck a 9-story residential building in central Chernihiv around midday on August 24, injuring at least 20 people including 3 children, in the third wave of Russian strikes on the city that day. A fire broke out on the building's ground floor. Chernihiv Oblast Governor Viacheslav Chaus called it a 'cynical strike by Russian terrorists on a residential building in Chernihiv — right in the middle of the day, on Independence Day.'

media.caption: Emergency responders at the residential building struck in central Chernihiv

title: Zelensky: Ukraine 'Already Defeating Russia' Through Resilience, Won't Cede Donbas to Save Kremlin 'Half a Million Soldiers'
detail: In his Independence Day address marking 35 years since Ukraine's break from the Soviet Union, President Zelensky said Ukraine wants peace but will not simply surrender, declaring 'we are already defeating Russia: through willpower, technology, resilience and dignity.' He told Russians their president is mortal and running out of time, and said Ukraine 'will not save the Kremlin half a million soldiers' by ceding the Donbas region. Zelensky called on allies to 'give Ukraine everything it needs to stop this war, to stop it faster than Putin can start the next one.' British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Council President António Costa attended the Kyiv commemorations.

media.caption: President Zelensky delivers Ukraine's 35th Independence Day address

title: Ukraine Hits 66 Russian Targets Overnight, Including Rostov Rocket-Fuel Plant and a MiG-29
detail: Ukrainian drones struck 66 targets across Russia and occupied territory overnight into August 24, commander Robert 'Madyar' Brovdi said. Targets included three Ozon logistics warehouses in Dagestan, Stavropol Krai, and Adygea (Ozon shares fell 12% after the strikes); the Kombinat Kamenskiy defense-industrial plant in Kamensk-Shakhtinsky, Rostov Oblast, which produces solid rocket fuel for Uragan, Smerch, and Tornado-S multiple-launch rocket systems; a MiG-29 fighter jet near Dolotinka, Rostov Oblast; four radar systems; a SOBR special police base in occupied Strilkove, Kherson Oblast; energy facilities in occupied Ukrainian territory; and two Russian 'shadow fleet' vessels in the Black Sea. Debris from an intercepted Ukrainian drone struck a childcare center in Krasnodar, killing 2 children and injuring 9 others, according to Russian officials.
